item.title: A for concept, C- for execution
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

First problem: The red herrings don't work. The reader is meant to believe that the "monster" is 173 until the reveal at the end; but its behaviour as described doesn't match 173 at all. Its speed isn't stated, but I think it's fair to assume that 173 is fast enough to kill you in one or maybe two blinks, at least from the other side of its containment area. It's not clear what distance "the monster" starts from, but it definitely makes no sense for the D-class to be alive after blinking multiple times, let alone after falling asleep, especially when it was already pressed against him by the time he fell asleep. It also makes no sense for 173 to go around him. So the reader is either going to 1) realize immediately that it's not 173; or 2) think that the writer is being sloppy in their depiction of 173. Sure, they might 3) think that the Foundation is performing an experiment that's making 173 act strangely (which I assume was your goal); or 4) 173 has some unknown reason for killing him slowly; but it takes more finesse to elicit that reaction, and the first two reactions are always a risk regardless. If there were only a few minor discrepancies, then it might work, but the behaviour described is a major departure from 173's whole schtick.

Second problem: The truth doesn't completely work, either. In fairness, a lot of the details do make sense once you realize it's 015; not just the discrepancies mentioned above, but also things like the cold sensation on his back. But, for example, how can 015 be both fast enough to visibly grow in the fraction of a second it takes to blink, yet slow enough to not kill him when he sleeps for more than a few minutes? Perhaps it doesn't visibly grow, and he's only aware of its growth because of the cumulative effect of many blinks; but if that's the case, it should be clearer. It would help to be given some sense of distances.

Third problem: As a corollary to the above, the detail of it having a "face", and the D-class calling it a "monster", while technically plausible, are a bit too misleading, and simply don't ring true. The reader feels cheated, not impressed by the clever smokescreen. It would be better to just remove those details entirely.

Fourth problem: Bait-and-switch only works if both the bait and the switch are recognizable to the reader. The bait is poorly set up, but is still easily serviceable because 173 is not only a Heritage SCP, but basically the poster child for this site. 015, however, was one I'm not sure I had even heard of before reading this. In any case, I wasn't familiar with it. So instead of being blown away by the twist, I was simply confused. I assumed that 173 had somehow attacked the D-class with a pipe. I had to read the comments to understand what I was supposed to take away from the ending. Even now that I know, it feels more like an "And Then I Died" mystery than a bait and switch. However, that might be on me, as I'm only an occasional reader; maybe the more faithful readers are abundantly familiar with 015. This is part of why I give the execution a C- instead of an F.

The other reason I don't give it an F is that, as I alluded to above, the story does technically make more sense once you realize it's 015. The slowness makes sense, the "monster" going "around" him makes sense, the cold on his back makes sense. Apart from the problem of 015 being both fast and slow, the details mostly fall into place nicely. So I don't view this story as a failure. I do, however, view it as a rough draft.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The pipes grow when not under observation. When he blinks, he's not observing them. That's why it's dangerous to sleep, and why it moves slowly enough that it doesn't kill him when he's asleep.

The face bit was a bit of a stretch though, as was calling it a "monster". While it's true the pipes can be made of things like human flesh, and that someone in this guy's position might call a mass of growing pipes "a monster", that part was just a bit too misleading and just doesn't ring true.

item.content:encoded:
You've got too much bait, not enough switch.

If it's the pipes, there's no reason for a face, and it's very strange to have it described as a "monster".

When you spend that long selling it as one thing you have to be very very careful that it still makes sense as what you switch it to; and it just doesn't. Reading it through knowing that it's the pipes the story doesn't make sense to me.
